chunks: 'Ali b. Ahmad b. Musa al-Daqqaq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Abi 'Abdillah al-Kufi al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Ismail al-Barmaki narrated to me from Ja'far b. Ahmad al-Kufi al-Bazzaz. He said: Ismail b. 'Abd al-Khaliq narrated to us from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (peace be upon them both), that he said:
Fasting Sha'ban and the month of Ramadan is repentance (forgiveness) from Allah, even from forbidden blood.

key_terms.تَوْبَةٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ: Repentance/forgiveness from Allah — divine acceptance and pardon
key_terms.دَمٍ حَرَامٍ: Prohibited blood — the unlawful taking of human life, considered among the gravest sins
key_terms.صَوْمُ شَعْبَانَ: Fasting of Sha'ban — the month preceding Ramadan; fasting it was a Sunnah of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: Does fasting Sha'ban and Ramadan forgive even major sins like shedding forbidden blood?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) declares that fasting the month of Sha'ban combined with fasting Ramadan brings divine forgiveness from Allah, even for the gravest of sins such as the unlawful shedding of blood. This hadith emphasizes the extraordinary spiritual power of these two consecutive fasting months in wiping away sins. The statement was delivered in the context of an assembly held twelve nights before the end of Sha'ban in 368 AH, underscoring the urgency of seizing this blessed season.
